question_content: A company has implemented one of its microservices on AWS Lambda that accesses an Amazon DynamoDB table named "Books". A solutions architect is designing an IAM policy to be attached to the Lambda function's IAM role giving it access to put, update, and delete items in the "Books" table. The IAM policy must prevent the function from performing any other actions on the "Books" table and any other table.Which IAM policy would fulfill these needs and provide the LEAST privileged access?

answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. This policy will provide the required Put, Update, and Delete actions to only the "Books" table.For more information about DynamoDB IAM policies, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/using-identity-based-policies.html#access-policy-examples-for-sdk-cli.example3Using Identity-Based Policies (IAM Policies) with Amazon DynamoDB.
Incorrect. This policy will provide the required Put, Update, and Delete actions to all the tables within the account.
Incorrect. This policy will provide all DynamoDB actions to the "Books" table. This policy will not restrict the Lambda function to Put, Update, and Delete actions.

Incorrect. The statement with the explicit deny will override the statement with the explicit allow. An explicit deny will always override an explicit allow.For more information about IAM policy logic, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.htmlPolicy Evaluation Logic.

question_content: An administrator wants to apply a resource-based policy to the S3 bucket named "iam-policy-testbucket" to restrict access and to allow accounts to only write objects to the bucket. When the administrator tries to apply the following policy to the "iam-policy-testbucket" bucket, the S3 bucket presents an error. { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Id": "Policy1646946718956", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "Stmt1646946717210", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::iam-policy-testbucket/*" } ]} How can the administrator correct the policy to resolve the error and successfully apply the policy?

answer_choices.choice_content: Change the Action element from s3:PutObject to s3:*.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You would not resolve the policy error by changing the Action element. Both s3:PutObject and s3:* are acceptable action statements.

answer_choices.choice_content: Remove the Resource element because it is unnecessary for resource-based policies.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You would cause additional errors by removing the Resource element because every IAM policy, identity-based and resource-based, requires a resource statement.

answer_choices.choice_content: Change the Resource element to NotResource.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You would cause the opposite effect to what the administrator wants to accomplish by changing the Resource element to NotResource. This solution would deny write access to this specific bucket.

answer_choices.choice_content: Add a Principal element to the policy to declare which accounts have access.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Resource-based policies must include a Principal element in the policy.For more information about resource-based polices, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_resource-basedResource-Based Policies.

question_content: A company designs a mobile app for its customers to upload photos to a website. The app needs a secure login with multi-factor authentication (MFA). The company wants to limit the initial build time and the maintenance of the solution.Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Cognito Identity with SMS-based MFA.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Amazon Cognito user pools are user directories that provide sign-up and sign-in options for web users and mobile app users. You can add MFA to Amazon Cognito user pools for secondary validation.For more information about Amazon Cognito, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-scenarios.htmlCommon Amazon Cognito Scenarios. For more information about MFA SMS text messages for users, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-settings-mfa-sms-text-message.htmlSMS Text Message MFA.

answer_choices.choice_content: Edit IAM policies to require MFA for all users.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The process of editing IAM policies for each user is time-consuming and ongoing work as new users start to use the mobile app. Moreover, the company wants to limit the initial build time. Creation and management of IAM users would be a high-maintenance solution.For more information about the creation of IAM policies, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_create.htmlCreating IAM Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Federate IAM against the corporate Active Directory that requires MFA.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. When you design a public application that has a growing number of users, it is best practice to federate. However, Active Directory does not provide the sign-up feature of Amazon Cognito.For more information about how to confirm users for Amazon Cognito, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/signing-up-users-in-your-app.htmlSigning Up and Confirming User Accounts.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon API Gateway and require server-side encryption (SSE) for photos.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although API Gateway supports in-transit and at-rest SSE for secure upload of photos, this solution does not address the need for MFA. The question is about secured login and MFA.For more information about data encryption in API Gateway, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/data-protection-encryption.htmlData encryption in Amazon API Gateway.

question_content: A solutions architect is designing a new workload in which an AWS Lambda function will access an Amazon DynamoDB table.What is the MOST secure means of granting the Lambda function access to the DynamoDB table?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an IAM role with the necessary permissions to access the DynamoDB table. Assign the role to the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. An IAM role is an IAM entity that defines a set of permissions for making AWS service requests. IAM roles are not associated with a specific user or group. Instead, trusted entities such as IAM users, applications, or AWS services assume roles.For more information about IAM roles, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.htmlIAM roles.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a DynamoDB user name and password and give them to the developer to use in the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. DynamoDB has no concept of user names or passwords. You can grant access to the Lambda function by using an IAM role.For more information about DynamoDB, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.htmlWhat Is Amazon DynamoDB?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an IAM user, and create access and secret keys for the user. Give the user the necessary permissions to access the DynamoDB table. Have the developer use these keys to access the resources.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The use of static keys in code makes it possible to compromise access to the environment. This solution is not a secure way for the Lambda function to access DynamoDB. This solution also is not scalable because the keys must be shared with every user.For more information about IAM users, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_users.htmlIAM users.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an IAM role allowing access from AWS Lambda. Assign the role to the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The IAM role should be assigned to the Lambda function. The Lambda function then would use that role to access DynamoDB. This response reverses that logic.For more information about IAM roles, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.htmlIAM roles.

question_content: A company has an application running as a service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the Amazon EC2 launch type. The application code makes AWS API calls to publish messages to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS).What is the MOST secure method of giving the application permission to publish messages to Amazon SQS?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to grant SQS permissions to the role used by the launch configuration for the Auto Scaling group of the ECS cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This method would work, but it is not secure enough. The addition of SQS permissions to the role used by the EC2 host means that all containers (including those of other services) that run on the host would inherit that access. A security compromise could result.For more information about launch configurations, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/us-iam-role.htmlIAM role for applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a new IAM user with SQS permissions. Then update the task definition to declare the access key ID and secret access key as environment variables.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This method would work, but it is not secure enough because the secrets would be in the task definition. The task definition is viewable by all users who have access to Amazon ECS.For more information about AWS Secrets Manager, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.htmlWhat is AWS Secrets Manager?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a new IAM role with SQS permissions. Then update the task definition to use this role for the task role setting.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The creation of a new IAM role (based on the minimal Amazon Elastic Container Service Task Role template) ensures that only the containers that are created with this task will receive access to Amazon SQS.For more information about IAM roles for tasks, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.htmlIAM Roles for Tasks.

answer_choices.choice_content: Update the security group used by the ECS cluster to allow access to Amazon SQS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Security groups do not control access to managed AWS services such as Amazon SQS. Instead, security groups control incoming traffic to instances and outgoing traffic from instances.For more information about security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.htmlAmazon EC2 security groups for Linux instances.

question_content:
A solutions architect needs to allow developers to have SSH connectivity to web servers. The requirements are as follows:/p
ul
  liLimit access to users originating from the corporate network./li
  liWeb servers cannot have SSH access directly from the internet./li
  liWeb servers reside in a private subnet./li
/ul
pWhich combination of steps must the architect complete to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a bastion host that authenticates users against the corporate directory.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A bastion host meets the requirement to prevent direct SSH access from the internet. However, simple authentication of users against the corporate directory would not prevent those users from logging in to the bastion host from a location outside the corporate network.For more information about bastion hosts, see https://aws.amazon.com/quickstart/architecture/linux-bastion/.Linux Bastion Hosts on AWS.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a bastion host with security group rules that only allow traffic from the corporate network.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. A bastion host meets the requirement to prevent direct SSH access from the internet. The addition of a security group rule that only allows SSH access from the corporate network meets the requirement to limit access accordingly.For more information about bastion hosts, see https://aws.amazon.com/quickstart/architecture/linux-bastion/Linux Bastion Hosts on AWS. For more information about security group rules, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html#SecurityGroupRulesSecurity group rules.

answer_choices.choice_content: Attach an IAM role to the bastion host with relevant permissions.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The IAM permissions that are assigned to a bastion host would not prevent users from logging in to the host from locations outside the corporate network. A role that is assigned to an instance would control what AWS API calls that instance can perform.For more information about bastion hosts, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quickstart/latest/linux-bastion/architecture.htmlLinux Bastion Hosts on the AWS Cloud: Quick Start Reference Deployment. For more information about IAM permissions for Amazon EC2, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.htmlIAM roles for Amazon EC2.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure the web servers' security group to allow SSH traffic from a bastion host.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The configuration of the web servers' security group to only allow SSH access from the bastion host will prevent access from other systems.For more information about security group rules, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html#SecurityGroupRulesSecurity group rules.

answer_choices.choice_content: Deny all SSH traffic from the corporate network in the inbound network ACL.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution fails to solve the problem because the Deny statement would block external traffic only from the corporate network. This solution would not prevent users from outside the corporate network from attempting to access the web server directly. Even if the instance were in a private subnet, this solution would not block SSH access from any other instance. Therefore, sideways SSH traffic would be permitted.For more information about network ACL rules, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html#nacl-rulesNetwork ACL rules.

question_content: A company hosts a popular web application. The web application connects to a database running in a private VPC subnet. The web servers must be accessible only to customers on an SSL connection. The Amazon RDS for MySQL database server must be accessible only from the web servers. How should a solutions architect design a solution to meet the requirements without impacting running applications?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a network ACL on the web server's subnet, and allow HTTPS inbound and MySQL outbound. Place both database and web servers on the same subnet.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution would cause the database to be accessible from the internet, which does not meet the requirements in the scenario.For more information about network ACLs, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.htmlNetwork ACLs. For more information about the differences between network ACLs and security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Security.htmlInternetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC.

answer_choices.choice_content: Open an HTTPS port on the security group for web servers and set the source to 0.0.0.0/0. Open the MySQL port on the database security group and attach it to the MySQL instance. Set the source to web server security group.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. If you leave the database in a private subnet and leave the web server in a public subnet, you restrict internet access to only the application server. One security group for each tier enforces least-privilege access. Security groups are stateful. Therefore, if a path is opened, then the return path is also open.For more information about security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.htmlSecurity groups for your VPC. For more information about network ACLs, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.htmlNetwork ACLs. For more information about differences between network ACLs and security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Security.htmlInternetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a network ACL on the web server's subnet; allow HTTPS inbound, and specify the source as 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL on a database subnet, allow MySQL port inbound for web servers, and deny all outbound traffic.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. If you set network ACLs on the subnet that contains the web servers, you open the permissions to any other instances in that subnet. You should avoid that action unless you are sure that no other servers are hosted in the subnet. However, the most critical flaw in this design is that all outbound traffic is denied from the database subnet. Network ACLs are stateless. Therefore, responses to allowed inbound traffic are subject to the rules for outbound traffic.For more information about network ACLs, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.htmlNetwork ACLs. For more information about differences between network ACLs and security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Security.htmlInternetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC.

answer_choices.choice_content: Open the MySQL port on the security group for web servers and set the source to 0.0.0.0/0. Open the HTTPS port on the database security group and attach it to the MySQL instance. Set the source to web server security group.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not helpful to open a MySQL port for the web servers because the web servers must receive HTTPS traffic. Likewise, it is not helpful to open the HTTPS ports for the database servers because the database servers must process traffic on the MySQL port.For more information about security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.htmlSecurity groups for your VPC. For more information about differences between network ACLs and security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Security.htmlInternetwork traffic privacy in Amazon VPC.

question_content: A company is performing an AWS Well-Architected Framework review of an existing workload deployed on AWS. The review identified a public-facing website running on the same Amazon EC2 instance as a Microsoft Active Directory domain controller that was installed recently to support other AWS services. A solutions architect needs to recommend a new design that would improve the security of the architecture and minimize the administrative demand on IT staff.What should the solutions architect recommend?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS Managed Microsoft AD to create a managed Active Directory. Uninstall Active Directory on the current EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. AWS Managed Microsoft AD is powered by an actual Microsoft Windows Server Active Directory that AWS manages in the AWS Cloud. This configuration reduces administrative overhead and is secure. Additionally, you can mitigate security risks by uninstalling Active Directory from the current server so the Active Directory and the website are not on the same server.For more information about AWS Managed Active Directory, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_microsoft_ad.htmlAWS Managed Microsoft AD.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create another EC2 instance in the same subnet and reinstall Active Directory on it. Uninstall Active Directory on the current EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. While this solution is technically feasible, it does not meet the requirement to minimize administrative demand on IT staff. Additionally, this solution creates the new Active Directory instance in the same subnet as the public-facing website, which is a security risk.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS Directory Service to create an Active Directory connector. Proxy Active Directory requests to the Active Directory domain controller running on the current EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The current architecture introduces a security risk by hosting both the Active Directory and the public-facing website on the same EC2 instance. The current architecture also does not reduce the administrative demand, as outlined in the scenario.For more information about how to use AD Connector, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/best-practices-deploying-amazon-workspaces/scenario-1-using-ad-connector-to-proxy-authentication-to-on-premises-active-directory-service.htmlScenario 1: Using AD Connector to Proxy Authentication to On-Premises Active Directory Service.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) with Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 federation with the current Active Directory controller. Modify the EC2 instance's security group to deny public access to Active Directory.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although it is technically possible to use IAM Identity Center and SAML, security groups permit only allow rule statements, not deny. Additionally, a solution that blocks public access to the current EC2 instance would also block traffic to the public-facing website.For more information about security groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.htmlControl Traffic to Resources Using Security Groups.

question_content: A company is reviewing a recent migration of a three-tier application to a VPC. The security team discovers that the principle of least privilege is not being applied to Amazon EC2 security group ingress and egress rules between the application tiers. What should a solutions architect do to correct this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create security group rules using the instance ID as the source or destination.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Security group rules are used to control inbound and outbound traffic that can reach instances associated with a security group. You cannot specify an instance ID as a source or destination in a security group.For more information about about security group rules, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules.htmlSecurity Group Rules.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create security group rules using the security group ID as the source or destination.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Security group rules are used to control inbound and outbound traffic that can reach instances associated with a security group. You can specify the security group ID as the source or destination. This solution ensures that the security group rules are implemented correctly and that application tiers are able to communicate.For more information about security group rules, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules.htmlSecurity Group Rules.For more information about controlling traffic to AWS resources, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-security-groups.htmlControl Traffic to Your AWS Resources Using Security Groups.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create security group rules using the VPC CIDR blocks as the source or destination.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. VPC CIDR blocks are groups of IP addresses that are assigned to your VPC. Although this solution is scoped to a private VPC address space, that space is shared with other applications. The other applications may not need access to the hosted application services. Therefore, this solution does not follow the principle of least privilege.For more information about VPC CIDR blocks, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-cidr-blocks.htmlVPC CIDR Blocks.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create security group rules using the subnet CIDR blocks as the source or destination.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Subnet CIDR blocks are groups of IP addresses that are assigned to a specific subnet within your VPC. Although it is possible to create security group rules by using the subnet CIDR blocks as the source or destination, it would not follow the principle of least privilege. This is because other applications in the VPC subnet may not need access to the hosted application.For more information about subnet CIDR blocks, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/subnet-sizing.htmlSubnet CIDR Blocks.

question_content: A solutions architect is designing a secure cloud-based application that uses Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC. The application uses other supported AWS services within the same Region. The network traffic between the instances and AWS services must remain private and must not travel across the public internet. Which service or resource will meet the security requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?

answer_choices.choice_content: Internet gateway
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. An internet gateway gives resources that are in a VPC public subnet (such as EC2 instances) the ability to connect to the internet. Traffic from the VPC would go through the internet to the other services within the Region. This solution would not keep the traffic private.For more information about internet gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.htmlConnect to the Internet Using an Internet Gateway.

answer_choices.choice_content: NAT gateway
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can use a NAT gateway to provide internet access to instances that are in a private subnet. However, the traffic would still travel over the public network after the traffic leaves the NAT gateway. This solution is not the most operationally efficient.For more information about NAT gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.htmlNAT Gateways.

answer_choices.choice_content: VPC endpoint
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. VPC endpoints are virtual devices that make communication possible between services in your VPC and supported AWS services without the need to use the public internet. This solution provides a private path between your VPC and other AWS services.For more information about VPC endpoints, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints.htmlAWS PrivateLink Concepts.

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Direct Connect
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although Direct Connect provides a private network connection to AWS and your VPC, Direct Connect is a networking service between your on-premises facilities and AWS.For more information about Direct Connect, see https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/features/AWS Direct Connect Features.

question_content: An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. The load balancer is in public subnets. The EC2 instances are in private subnets and must not be accessible from the internet. The EC2 instances must call external services on the internet. Each Availability Zone must be able to call the external services, regardless of the status of the other Availability Zones.How should these requirements be met?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a NAT gateway attached to the VPC. Add a route to the gateway that connects to each private subnet route table.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Unlike internet gateways, which apply to the entire VPC, NAT gateways must reside within a subnet and within a single Availability Zone. The use of a single NAT gateway would result in a single point of failure.For more information about NAT gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonVPC/latest/UserGuide/vpc-nat-gateway.html#nat-gateway-basicsNAT gateway basics.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure an internet gateway. Add a route to the gateway that connects to each private subnet route table.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution would turn the private subnets into public subnets and would make the EC2 instances accessible from the internet.For more information about internet gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.htmlInternet gateways.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a NAT instance in the private subnet of each Availability Zone. Update the route tables for each private subnet to direct internet-bound traffic to the NAT instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. To securely route traffic from private subnets to the internet, you must create NAT instances in public subnets.For more information about NAT instances, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_NAT_Instance.htmlNAT instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone. Update the route tables for each private subnet to direct internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. A NAT gateway is assigned to a public subnet and is associated with a single Availability Zone. This solution ensures that each Availability Zone is independent of the others for internet routing.For more information about NAT gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonVPC/latest/UserGuide/vpc-nat-gateway.html#nat-gateway-basicsNAT gateway basics.

question_content: An application running in a private subnet accesses an Amazon DynamoDB table. The data cannot leave the AWS network to meet security requirements.How should this requirement be met?

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a network ACL on DynamoDB to limit traffic to the private subnet.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Because DynamoDB is serverless, it does not reside in a VPC. Therefore, there are no network ACLs to configure.For more information about DynamoDB, see https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/Amazon DynamoDB.

answer_choices.choice_content: Enable DynamoDB encryption at rest using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Encryption of the data connection between the application and DynamoDB does not affect how traffic is routed. Therefore, this solution would not prevent traffic from being routed outside the private subnet.For more information about data protection in DynamoDB, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/data-protection.htmlData Protection in DynamoDB.

answer_choices.choice_content: Add a NAT gateway and configure the route table on the private subnet.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A NAT gateway gives instances in a private subnet the ability to connect to the internet. This solution would not prevent traffic from being routed outside the private subnet.For more information about NAT gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.htmlNAT gateways.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and configure the endpoint policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. With an endpoint inside the VPC and routing to that endpoint, traffic that is destined for DynamoDB would not leave the network.For more information about how to use VPC endpoints to access DynamoDB, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/vpc-endpoints-dynamodb.htmlUsing Amazon VPC Endpoints to Access DynamoDB. For more information in this tutorial about how to configure a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/vpc-endpoints-dynamodb-tutorial.htmlTutorial: Using a VPC Endpoint for DynamoDB.

question_content: A company wants to create an application that will transmit protected health information (PHI) to thousands of service consumers in different AWS accounts. The application servers will sit in private VPC subnets. The routing for the application must be fault tolerant.What should be done to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a VPC endpoint service and grant permissions to specific service consumers to create a connection.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. With a VPC endpoint, you can privately connect your VPC to supported AWS services and VPC endpoint services powered by AWS PrivateLink without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect connection. Instances in your VPC do not require public IP addresses to communicate with resources in the service. Traffic between your VPC and the other service does not leave the Amazon network.For more information about VPC endpoints, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonVPC/latest/UserGuide/endpoint-service.htmlVPC endpoint services (AWS PrivateLink).

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a virtual private gateway connection between each pair of service provider VPCs and service consumer VPCs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A virtual private gateway gives a VPC access to and from the internet. The incorporation of a virtual private gateway in the architecture would make the private subnets into public subnets. In addition, you cannot use virtual private gateways in the way that this response describes.For more information about virtual private gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/how_it_works.html#VPNGatewayHow AWS Site-to-Site VPN works.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an internal Application Load Balancer in the service provider VPC and put application servers behind it.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets, such as Amazon EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses, in one or more Availability Zones. An ALB does not route traffic to AWS services in a different account.For more information about ALBs, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.htmlWhat is an Application Load Balancer?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a proxy server in the service provider VPC to route requests from service consumers to the application servers.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. In this solution, the company would use a proxy server as a gateway between users and the internet. This solution is neither scalable nor fault tolerant.

question_content: A company is planning to use Amazon S3 to store images uploaded by its users. The images must be encrypted at rest in Amazon S3. The company does not want to spend time managing and rotating the keys, but it does want to control who can access those keys.What should a solutions architect use to accomplish this?

answer_choices.choice_content: Server-Side Encryption with encryption keys stored in an S3 bucket
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that stores the encryption keys in an S3 bucket would require the customer to rotate and manage access to the keys.For more information about Amazon S3 security best practices, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html#security-best-practices-preventAmazon S3 Preventative Security Best Practices.

answer_choices.choice_content: Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C)
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. SSE-C requires the customer to manage the encryption keys. In this scenario, the customer does not want to manage the keys. Amazon S3 does not store, rotate, or manage access to the encryption keys.

answer_choices.choice_content: Server-Side Encryption with encryption keys stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that stores the encryption keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store would require the customer to rotate the keys.For more information about AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.htmlAWS Systems Manager Parameter Store/span/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS-Managed Keys (SSE-KMS)
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. SSE-KMS uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create, manage, rotate, and control access to encryption keys.For more information about SSE-KMS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.htmlUsing Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS Keys (SSE-KMS). For more information about AWS KMS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.htmlAWS Key Management Service.

question_content: A company's legacy application is currently relying on a single-instance Amazon RDS MySQL database without encryption. Due to new compliance requirements, all existing and new data in this database must be encrypted.How should this be accomplished?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with server-side encryption turned on. Move all the data to Amazon S3. Delete the RDS instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon RDS MySQL database instances support encryption. Additionally, Amazon S3 might not be a viable replacement for Amazon RDS. For more information about how to encrypt Amazon RDS resources, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.htmlEncrypting Amazon RDS Resources. For more information about Amazon S3, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.htmlWhat Is Amazon S3?

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure RDS Multi-AZ mode with encryption at rest turned on. Perform a failover to the standby instance to delete the original instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not possible to create an encrypted standby DB instance from an unencrypted primary DB instance.

answer_choices.choice_content: Take a snapshot of the RDS instance. Create an encrypted copy of the snapshot. Restore the RDS instance from the encrypted snapshot.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. You can configure encryption for an RDS DB instance only when you create the DB instance. Alternatively, you can create a snapshot of the RDS instance. Next, you create an encrypted copy of the snapshot. Finally, you can create an RDS instance from the encrypted snapshot.For more information about RDS encrypted DB instances, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html#Overview.Encryption.LimitationsLimitations of Amazon RDS encrypted DB instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an RDS read replica with encryption at rest turned on. Promote the read replica to primary and switch the application over to the new primary. Delete the old RDS instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not possible to create an encrypted read replica of an unencrypted DB instance or an unencrypted read replica of an encrypted DB instance.

question_content: A company currently operates a web application backed by an Amazon RDS MySQL database. It has automated backups that run daily and are not encrypted. A security audit requires future backups to be encrypted and the unencrypted backups to be destroyed. The company will make at least one encrypted backup before destroying the old backups.What should be done to set up encryption for future backups?

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on default encryption for the Amazon S3 bucket where backups are stored.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Users do not have access to the S3 bucket that stores Amazon RDS automated backups. Therefore, users can not turn on encryption for this bucket.For more information about Amazon RDS backups, see https://aws.amazon.com/rds/features/backup/Amazon RDS Backup and Restore.

answer_choices.choice_content: Modify the backup section of the database configuration to toggle the Enable encryption check box.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not possible to create an encrypted backup of an unencrypted DB instance. You can configure encryption for a DB instance only when you initially create the DB instance.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a snapshot of the database. Copy it to an encrypted snapshot. Restore the database from the encrypted snapshot.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. You cannot create an encrypted snapshot of an unencrypted DB instance. However, you can encrypt a copy of the unencrypted snapshot and restore the snapshot to a new DB instance.For more information about how to encrypt RDS snapshots, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.htmlEncrypting Amazon RDS Resources.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure an encrypted read replica on RDS for MySQL. Promote the encrypted read replica to primary. Remove the original database instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not possible to create an encrypted read replica of an unencrypted DB instance.

question_content: A company's cloud operations team wants to standardize resource remediation. The company wants to provide a standard set of governance evaluations and remediations to all member accounts in its organization in AWS Organizations.Which self-managed AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Security Hub compliance standards
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Security Hub is a managed service that provides you with a comprehensive view of your security state in AWS and helps you check your environment against security industry standards and best practices. The scenario requires a standard set of governance evaluations, not just security.For more information about Security Hub, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/what-is-securityhub.htmlWhat is AWS Security Hub?/span

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Config conformance packs
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. AWS Config conformance packs are collections of AWS Config rules and remediation actions that you can deploy as a single entity in an account and a Region or across an organization in AWS Organizations.For more information about conformance packs for AWS Config, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/conformance-packs.htmlConformance Packs. For more information about AWS Config, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.htmlWhat is AWS Config?/span

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS CloudTrail
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. CloudTrail records API calls but does not make recommendations or provide remediation. CloudTrail helps you facilitate governance, compliance, and operational and risk auditing of your AWS account.For more information about CloudTrail, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.htmlWhat is AWS CloudTrail?

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Trusted Advisor
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Trusted Advisor is an online tool that provides you with real-time guidance to help you provision your resources according to AWS best practices. Trusted Advisor does not provide remediation.For more information about Trusted Advisor, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.htmlAWS Trusted Advisor.

question_content: An application launched on Amazon EC2 instances needs to publish personally identifiable information (PII) about customers using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). The application is launched in private subnets within an Amazon VPC.What is the MOST secure way to allow the application to access service endpoints in the same AWS Region?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an internet gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The use of an internet gateway would require a public IP address on the application instances. Therefore, this solution is not the most secure option.For more information about internet gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.htmlInternet gateways.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS PrivateLink.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The use of PrivateLink does not require a public IP address on the instances or public access from the instance subnet. Traffic remains within the Region of the VPC and provides no single point of failure with the VPC endpoint. PrivateLink is the feature that powers VPC endpoints.For more information about VPC endpoints and Amazon SNS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-vpc.htmlInternetwork traffic privacy.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use a NAT gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The use of a NAT gateway would allow application traffic to travel outside the VPC and over the internet to reach the service endpoints. Therefore, this solution is not the most secure option.For more information about NAT gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.htmlNAT gateways.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use a proxy instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The use of a proxy instance would require the provisioning of an EC2 instance and would introduce a single point of failure in the application architecture. In addition, application traffic would traverse the public internet. Therefore, this solution is not the most secure option.For more information about how to use an HTTP proxy, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-proxy.htmlUsing an HTTP proxy.

question_content: An application running on AWS Lambda requires an API key to access a third-party service. The key must be stored securely with audited access to the Lambda function only. What is the MOST secure way to store the key?

answer_choices.choice_content: As an object in Amazon S3
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon S3 is a reliable and inexpensive service to store data, but it is not the most secure choice for storing credentials. Parameter Store is a better option for storing credentials.For more information about use cases for Amazon S3, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/S3-gsg-CommonUseScenarios.htmlCommon use scenarios.

answer_choices.choice_content: As a secure string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Parameter Store provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and secrets management. You can store data such as passwords, database strings, Amazon Machine Image (AMI) IDs, and license codes as parameter values. You can store values as plaintext or encrypted data. You can reference Systems Manager parameters in your scripts, commands, Systems Manager documents, and configuration and automation workflows by using the unique name that you specified when you created the parameter.For more information about Parameter Store, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-paramstore.htmlAWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. For more information about how Parameter Store uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/services-parameter-store.htmlHow AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store uses AWS KMS.

answer_choices.choice_content: Inside a file on an Amazon EBS volume attached to the Lambda function
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You cannot attach EBS volumes to Lambda functions. Even if you could attach EBS volumes to Lambda functions, Parameter Store is a better option for storing credentials.For more information about Lambda, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.htmlWhat is AWS Lambda?

answer_choices.choice_content: Inside a secrets file stored on Amazon EFS
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can mount an EFS file system to a Lambda function, but a file system is not the most secure option to store credentials. Parameter Store offers features such as change notification, tag-based access, and data validation.For more information about Amazon EFS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.htmlAmazon EFS: How it works.

question_content: A company is designing a website that will be hosted on Amazon S3. How should users be prevented from linking directly to the assets in the S3 bucket?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a static website, then update the bucket policy to require users to access the resources with the static website URL.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can use S3 bucket policies to grant permissions to S3 resources. However, the users still would be able to access the objects directly in the S3 bucket.For more information about S3 bucket policies, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.htmlUsing Bucket Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin access control (OAC) and update the bucket policy to grant permission to the OAC only.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. To restrict access to the assets in S3 buckets, you can create an OAC and associate it with the website distribution. You would configure the S3 bucket permissions so that CloudFront can use the OAC to access the files in the S3 bucket and serve the files to the users. Afterward, the users can access the static website files only through CloudFront, not directly from the S3 bucket.For more information about how to use an OAC to restrict access to S3 content, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.htmlRestricting Access to an Amazon S3 Origin.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a static website, then configure an Amazon Route 53 record set with an alias pointing to the static website. Provide this URL to users.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS web service. This solution still would allow the users to access the objects directly in the S3 bucket.For more information about Route 53, see https://aws.amazon.com/route53/faqs/Amazon Route 53 FAQs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an AWS WAF web ACL that permits access to the origin server through the distribution only.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS WAF will block or allow requests based on conditions that you specify, but the web ACL would not prevent the users from linking directly to the resources in the origin of the S3 bucket.For more information about AWS WAF, see https://aws.amazon.com/waf/faqs/AWS WAF FAQs.

question_content: A web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application allows users to create custom reports of historical weather data. Generating a report can take up to 5 minutes. These long-running requests use many of the available incoming connections, making the system unresponsive to other users.How can a solutions architect make the system more responsive?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon SQS with AWS Lambda to generate reports.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. If the company uses Amazon SQS and Lambda to offload the report generation, the system will no longer use resources on the web application servers to process the reports. Therefore, the system will no longer consume all the connections.For more information about how to use Amazon SQS to offload reports, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/operatorguide/integrations-asynchronous.htmlUsing service integrations and asynchronous processing.

answer_choices.choice_content: Increase the idle timeout on the ALB to 5 minutes.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution would affect only the connection between the ALB and the EC2 instances. This solution would not address timeouts between the client and the ALB. Additionally, this solution would exacerbate the problem of long-running requests that starve other connections.For more information about the idle timeout in an ALB, see https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/elb-idle-timeout-control/Elastic Load Balancing Connection Timeout Management.

answer_choices.choice_content: Update the client-side application code to increase its request timeout to 5 minutes.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution would affect only the connection between the client and the ALB. This solution would not affect the timeout between the ALB and the EC2 instances. Additionally, this solution would exacerbate the problem of long-running requests that starve other connections.

answer_choices.choice_content: Publish the reports to Amazon S3 and use Amazon CloudFront for downloading to the user.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. In this scenario, CloudFront will not help significantly because each report is custom generated. Therefore, cache hits will be rare. In addition, the creation of the report will still occur in the EC2 instances. This solution would not address the problem of long-running requests that starve other connections.

question_content:
An online photo application lets users upload photos and perform image editing operations. The application is built on Amazon EC2 instances and offers two classes of service: free and paid. Photos submitted by paid users are processed before those submitted by free users. Photos are uploaded to Amazon S3 and the job information is sent to Amazon SQS.
Which configuration should a solutions architect recommend?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use one SQS FIFO queue. Assign a higher priority to the photos from paid users so they are processed first.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Two separate queues are necessary to differentiate between paid and free requests. Prioritization would occur in the application that runs on the EC2 instances, not in Amazon SQS.For more information about the specific features of SQS queue types, see https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/features/Amazon SQS Features.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use two SQS FIFO queues: one for paid users and one for free users. Set the free queue to use short polling and the paid queue to use long polling.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although two separate queues are necessary, polling within SQS is not the correct solution for this situation.For more information about short and long polling, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-short-and-long-polling.htmlAmazon SQS Short and Long Polling.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use two SQS standard queues: one for paid users and one for free users. Configure the application on the Amazon EC2 instances to prioritize polling for the paid queue over the free queue.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Two separate queues are necessary for both free and paid requests. Prioritization would occur in the application that runs on the EC2 instances.For more information about standard queues, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.htmlAmazon SQS Standard Queues.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use one SQS standard queue. Set the visibility timeout of the photos from paid users to zero. Configure the application on the Amazon EC2 instances to prioritize visibility settings so photos from paid users are processed first.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Two separate queues are necessary for both free and paid requests. Visibility timeout is not related to queue prioritization.For information about visibility timeout, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.htmlAmazon SQS Visibility Timeout.

question_content: A company built a food ordering application that captures user data and stores it for future analysis. The application's static front-end is deployed on an Amazon EC2 instance. The front-end application sends the requests to the backend application running on a separate EC2 instance. The backend application then stores the data in Amazon RDS.What should a solutions architect do to decouple the architecture and make it scalable?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon S3 to serve the static front-end application, which sends requests to Amazon EC2 to run the backend application. The backend application will process and store the data in Amazon RDS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that uses one EC2 instance for the backend application is an example of a tightly coupled architecture. This solution cannot scale without additional architectural improvements such as an EC2 Auto Scaling group and/or an Elastic Load Balancer.For more information about Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 Auto Scaling, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.htmlUse Elastic Load Balancing to Distribute Traffic Across the Instances in Your Auto Scaling Group.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon S3 to serve the static front-end application and write requests to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the backend Amazon EC2 instance HTTP/S endpoint to the topic, and process and store the data in Amazon RDS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon SNS decouples the architecture and is scalable. However, messages that are published to the SNS topic are not stored and cannot be re-examined if processing fails. Additionally, a solution that uses one EC2 instance for the backend application is an example of a tightly coupled architecture. This type of solution cannot scale without additional architectural improvements such as an EC2 Auto Scaling group and/or an Elastic Load Balancer.For more information about Amazon SNS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.htmlWhat Is Amazon SNS? For more information about Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 Auto Scaling, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.htmlUse Elastic Load Balancing to Distribute Traffic Across the Instances in Your Auto Scaling Group.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an EC2 instance to serve the static front-end application and write requests to an Amazon SQS queue. Place the backend instance in an Auto Scaling group, and scale based on the queue depth to process and store the data in Amazon RDS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that uses one EC2 instance for the frontend application is an example of a tightly coupled architecture. This solution cannot scale without additional architectural improvements such as an EC2 Auto Scaling group and/or an Elastic Load Balancer.For more information about Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 Auto Scaling, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.htmlUse Elastic Load Balancing to Distribute Traffic Across the Instances in Your Auto Scaling Group.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon S3 to serve the static front-end application and send requests to Amazon API Gateway, which writes the requests to an Amazon SQS queue. Place the backend instances in an Auto Scaling group, and scale based on the queue length to process and store the data in Amazon RDS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. A solution that moves the static frontend application to Amazon S3 will decouple the frontend application from the backend application. This solution will allow for scalability and improve application availability by removing the EC2 instance as a single point of failure.A serverless managed services like API Gateway and Amazon SQS would also eliminate single points of failure and further decouple the frontend requests from processing operations. API Gateway is an AWS service that creates, publishes, maintains, monitors, and secures REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at any scale. Amazon SQS provides a highly available and scalable message queuing service.The addition of a backend EC2 instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group will improve backend scalability and remove another single point of failure.For more information about how to host static websites by using Amazon S3, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.htmlHosting a Static Website Using Amazon S3. For more information about API Gateway, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.htmlWhat Is Amazon API Gateway? For more information about Amazon SQS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.htmlWhat Is Amazon Simple Queue Service? For more information about EC2 Auto Scaling, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/GettingStartedTutorial.htmlGet Started with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling.

question_content: A media company has an application that tracks user clicks on its websites and performs analytics to provide near-real-time recommendations. The application has a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that receive data from the websites and send the data to an Amazon RDS DB instance for long-term retention. Another fleet of EC2 instances hosts the portion of the application that is continuously checking changes in the database and running SQL queries to provide recommendations.Management has requested a redesign to decouple the infrastructure. The solution must ensure that data analysts are writing SQL to analyze the new data only. No data can be lost during the deployment.What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements and to provide the FASTEST access to the user activity?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to capture the data from the websites, Kinesis Data Firehose to persist the data on Amazon S3, and Amazon Athena to query the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The use of Kinesis Data Firehose to persist the data to Amazon S3 meets the requirements. However, this solution is not the fastest way to access the data because the data is available only after Kinesis Data Firehose has written it to Amazon S3.For more information about Kinesis Data Firehose, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.htmlWhat is Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to capture the data from the websites, Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data, and Kinesis Data Firehose to persist the data on Amazon S3.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. This solution offers queries of the data before the data is sent to persistent storage. Kinesis Data Firehose retains the records for a default time of 24 hours if a replay is needed.For more information about Kinesis Data Firehose, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.htmlWhat is Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose? For more information about Kinesis Data Firehose, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/troubleshooting.htmlTroubleshooting Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to capture the data from the websites, keep the fleet of EC2 instances, and change to a bigger instance type in the Auto Scaling group configuration.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. An increase in instance size might improve performance, but you are still reading the data only after it is written to the database. A faster solution is to read the data before it is written to the database.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to receive data from the websites and proxy the messages to AWS Lambda functions that run the queries and persist the data. Change Amazon RDS to Amazon Aurora Serverless to persist the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon SNS does not durably store messages. If there were a problem with running the Lambda function, the data would be lost. In addition, you are still reading the data only after it is written to the database. A faster solution is to read the data before it is written to the database.

question_content: A solutions architect is redesigning a monolithic application to be a loosely coupled application composed of two microservices: Microservice A and Microservice B.Microservice A places messages in a main Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for Microservice B to consume. When Microservice B fails to process a message after four retries, the message needs to be removed from the queue and stored for further investigation.What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an SQS dead-letter queue. Microservice B adds failed messages to that queue after it receives and fails to process the message four times.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This is an incorrect design for dead-letter queues. A solution that adds failed messages to a dead-letter queue in this way will not remove messages from the original SQS queue.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an SQS dead-letter queue. Configure the main SQS queue to deliver messages to the dead-letter queue after the message has been received four times.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. This solution uses a redrive policy on the main SQS queue to send messages to a dead-letter queue after consumption fails a certain number of times.For more information about SQS dead-letter queues, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html#sqs-dead-letter-queues-how-they-workHow Do Dead-Letter Queues Work?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an SQS queue for failed messages. Microservice A adds failed messages to that queue after Microservice B receives and fails to process the message four times.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This is an incorrect design for dead-letter queues. Microservice A has no way to know whether Microservice B has failed to consume a message. Additionally, this solution does not meet the requirement to remove the message from the original SQS queue.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an SQS queue for failed messages. Configure the SQS queue for failed messages to pull messages from the main SQS queue after the original message has been received four times.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is not possible to configure a queue to retrieve failed messages from another queue.

question_content: A company has decided to use AWS to achieve high availability. The company's architecture consists of an Application Load Balancer in front of an Auto Scaling group that consists of Amazon EC2 instances. The company uses Amazon CloudWatch metrics and alarms to monitor the architecture. A solutions architect notices that the company is not able to launch some instances. The solutions architect finds the following message: EC2 QUOTA EXCEEDED. How can the solutions architect ensure that the company is able to launch all the EC2 instances correctly?

answer_choices.choice_content: Modify the Auto Scaling group to raise the maximum number of instances that the company can launch.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The Auto Scaling group upper limit is not the cause of the message. The Auto Scaling group would continue to launch instances until it reached the maximum number of instances available. The message does not mean the Auto Scaling group needs to raise its limit. For more information about how to set capacity limits, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-capacity-limits.htmlSet Capacity Limits on Your Auto Scaling Group.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Service Quotas to request an increase to the number of EC2 instances that the company can launch.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The message "EC2 QUOTA EXCEEDED" means that the company has reached the current limit for a service. To launch more resources, the company must use Service Quotas to request a limit increase.For more information about how to request an increase to a service limit, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-resource-limits.html#request-increaseRequest an Increase.

answer_choices.choice_content: Recreate the Auto Scaling group to ensure the Auto Scaling group is connected to the Application Load Balancer.

You would not resolve the error by recreating the Auto Scaling group because the EC2 service quota limit would still be the same.For more information about EC2 service quotas, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-resource-limits.htmlAmazon EC2 Service Quotas.

answer_choices.choice_content: Modify the CloudWatch metric that the company monitors to launch the instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. CloudWatch is not the cause of the message. You would not resolve the error by adjusting the CloudWatch metrics. The EC2 service quota would still be the same.For more information about EC2 service quotas, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-resource-limits.htmlAmazon EC2 Service Quotas.

question_content: A restaurant reservation application needs to access a waiting list. When a customer tries to reserve a table, and none are available, the customer application will put the user on the waiting list, and the application will notify the customer when a table becomes free. The waiting list must preserve the order in which customers were added to the waiting list.Which service should the solutions architect recommend to store this waiting list?

answer_choices.choice_content: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon SNS is a notification service. Notifications are immediate and are suitable for some needs. For this scenario, a queuing service is preferable because the queue message can be maintained until a table is available.For more information about Amazon SNS, see https://docs.amazonaws.cn/en_us/sns/latest/dg/welcome.htmlWhat is Amazon SNS?

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Step Functions invoking AWS Lambda functions
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Lambda functions time out in 15 minutes, so they would not work for this application. The Lambda function also bills for the time that the function is active and waiting for a table to become available.For more information about Lambda quotas, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.htmlLambda quotas.

answer_choices.choice_content: A FIFO queue in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Amazon SQS creates messages that exist in the queue until they are removed. A message would be created when a table is requested. The message would be removed when the table becomes available. FIFO queues respect the order in which items enter the queue. This solution would ensure that the person who has waited the longest for a table receives the next available table.For more information about Amazon SQS, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/Welcome.htmlWhat is Amazon Simple Queue Service? For more information about SQS FIFO queues, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.htmlAmazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queues.

answer_choices.choice_content: A standard queue in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A standard queue would hold the message and retain it until a table becomes available. However, this solution has no mechanism to make sure that the person who has waited the longest for a table receives the next available table. Standard queues do not respect the order in which items enter the queue.For more information about SQS standard queues, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.htmlAmazon SQS Standard queues.

question_content: A company has a web application that makes requests to a backend API service. The API service runs on Amazon EC2 instances accessed behind an Elastic Load Balancer.Most backend API service endpoint calls finish very quickly, but one endpoint that makes calls to create objects in an external service takes a long time to complete. answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to offload the long-running requests for asynchronous processing by separate workers.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. You can move the long-running calls off the interactive request path so that separate resources can complete them asynchronously. This solution ensures that your backend API service does not exhaust its incoming connection resources and limit normal client requests.For more information about request offloading with Amazon SQS, see https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/detailsAmazon SQS features (Using Amazon SQS with other AWS infrastructure web services section).

answer_choices.choice_content: Increase the load balancer idle timeout to allow the long-running requests to complete.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache responses from the external service.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A cache will not help here because the long-running call is a mutable operation. The long-running call is creating objects in the external service.For more information about ElastiCache for Redis, see https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/redis/Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.

question_content: A company runs a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an ELB Application Load Balancer. Amazon Route 53 is used for the DNS. answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon S3 website hosting for the backup website and a Route 53 failover routing policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Because the backup website uses static data, Amazon S3 is an ideal solution. For more information about failover routing, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.htmlFailover Routing.

If you select latency-based routing, then you will direct some customers who are physically near the backup website to Amazon S3 even if the primary website is operational.For more information about failover routing and latency-based routing, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.htmlChoosing a Routing Policy.

answer_choices.choice_content: Deploy the application in another AWS Region and use ELB health checks for failover routing.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The scope of an ELB is the Region within which you create the ELB. Additionally, you can register instances as targets by using the respective instance IDs of the targets only within the VPC that you specified for the target group.For more information about Availability Zones and load balancer nodes, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.htmlHow Elastic Load Balancing Works. For more information about how to register targets with a target group, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-register-targets.html#register-instancesRegister or deregister targets by instance ID.

answer_choices.choice_content: Deploy the application in another AWS Region and use server-side redirection on the primary website.

question_content: A company needs to implement a relational database with a multi-Region disaster recovery Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 1 second and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 1 minute.Which AWS solution can achieve this?

question_content: A solutions architect is designing a hybrid application using the AWS Cloud. The network between the on-premises data center and AWS will use an AWS Direct Connect (DX) connection. answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a DX connection with a VPN on top of it.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a DX connection using the most reliable DX partner.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure multiple virtual interfaces on top of a DX connection.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure DX connections at multiple DX locations.

You can achieve maximum resiliency for critical workloads by using separate connections that terminate on separate devices in more than one location.For more information about resilience in Direct Connect, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.htmlResilience in AWS Direct Connect.

question_content: A company wants to build an immutable infrastructure for its software applications. The company wants to test the software applications before sending traffic to them. question_content: During a review of business applications, a solutions architect identifies a critical application with a relational database that was built by a business user and is running on the user's desktop. answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the backend database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Migrate the application code to AWS Elastic Beanstalk.

For more information, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/Welcome.htmlWhat is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?

question_content: A team has an application that detects when new objects are uploaded into an Amazon S3 bucket. answer_choices.choice_content: Create a DynamoDB stream for the DynamoDB table.

question_content: A company is building a document storage application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. question_content: A company has a three-tier architecture solution in which an application writes to a relational database. Because of frequent requests, the company wants to cache data whenever the application writes data to the database. The company's priority is to minimize latency for data retrieval and to ensure that data in the cache is never stale. Which caching strategy should the company use to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Amazon ElastiCache with write-through
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The write-through strategy adds data or updates data that is in the cache whenever the application writes data to the database. Data in the cache is never stale because the data in the cache is updated every time the application writes the data to the database. ElastiCache supports relational databases.For more information about write-through, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Strategies.html#Strategies.WriteThroughWrite-Through.

answer_choices.choice_content: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
