answer_choices.choice_content: Amazon ElastiCache with lazy loading
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Lazy loading is a caching strategy that loads data into the cache only when necessary. If the application writes data to the cache only when there is a cache miss, then data in the cache can become stale. This result occurs because there are no updates to the cache when data changes in the database. ElastiCache supports relational databases.For more information about lazy loading, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/Strategies.html#Strategies.LazyLoadingLazy Loading.

question_content: An environment has an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones referred to as AZ-a and AZ-b. AZ-a has four Amazon EC2 instances, and AZ-b has three EC2 instances. If your application runs for less than 10 minutes, you will still pay the minimum charge. answer_choices.choice_content: Refactor the blog application to use Aurora parallel query.

This solution is not cost-effective because this solution will always run an instance, even when there is no application activity.For more information about how parallel queries work, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraFeaturesRegionsDBEngines.grids.html#Concepts.Aurora_Fea_Regions_DB-eng.Feature.ParallelQueryAurora Parallel Queries.

answer_choices.choice_content: Convert the original Aurora database to an Aurora global database.

answer_choices.choice_content: Convert the original Aurora database to Amazon Aurora Serverless.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. If you use Aurora Serverless, you pay for only the database resources that you consume on a per-second basis.For more information about Aurora Serverless use cases, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless.html#aurora-serverless.use-casesUsing Amazon Aurora Serverless v1.

question_content: A company wants to deploy an additional Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for development purposes. This cluster will be used several times a week for a few minutes upon request to debug production query issues. The company wants to keep overhead low for this resource. Which solution meets the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answer_choices.choice_content: Purchase a Reserved Instance for the DB instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Reserved Instances will reduce cost compared with On-Demand Instances, but this solution is not the most cost-effective answer.For more information about Aurora Reserved Instances, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_WorkingWithReservedDBInstances.htmlReserved DB instances for Aurora.

answer_choices.choice_content: Run the DB instances on Aurora Serverless.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Aurora Serverless is an on-demand, automatically scaling configuration for Aurora. Aurora Serverless automatically starts up, shuts down, and scales capacity based on an application's needs. It gives you the ability to run your database in the cloud without managing any database capacity. Serverless is the right solution for unpredictable workloads or workloads that have infrequent use.For more information about Aurora Serverless, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless.html#aurora-serverless.use-casesUse cases for Aurora Serverless v1.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a stop/start schedule for the DB instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The DB cluster will be accessed randomly during the day and will not be used all the time. The pattern is not consistent, so it is not possible to create a schedule for the start and stop actions.For more information about how to stop and restart a DB instance, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.htmlStopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an AWS Lambda function to stop DB instances if there are no active connections.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The company could use a Lambda function to stop the DB instances, but this solution includes no mechanism to restart the DB instances.For more information about how to stop and restart a DB instance, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.htmlStopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily.

question_content: A company has a well-architected application that streams audio data by using UDP in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the application in the eu-central-1 Region. The company plans to offer services to North American users. A solutions architect must improve application network performance for the North American users.Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective solution?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with an endpoint group in eu-central-1.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Global Accelerator improves TCP and UDP network performance for users around the world, even if a company hosts an application in only one Region. Global Accelerator routes application traffic to the nearest Global Accelerator edge location. Application traffic travels over the well-monitored, congestion-free, and redundant AWS global network to the endpoint. Global Accelerator optimizes the network path by maximizing the time that traffic is on the AWS network.For more information about Global Accelerator endpoint groups, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/work-with-standard-accelerators.htmlWork with Standard Accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy additional application infrastructure in the us-east-1 Region and the us-west-1 Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although CloudFormation incurs no costs, you pay for the resources that a CloudFormation template deploys inside your AWS account. You would triple overall operational costs by deploying the application in two additional Regions. Additional configuration would also be necessary to send traffic to the new Regions, such as a Route 53 geolocation, geoproximity, or latency routing policy.For more information about AWS CloudFormation, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.htmlWhat Is AWS CloudFormation?https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html /a

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and use the North America (United States, Mexico, Canada) and Europe and Israel price classes.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon CloudFront is a caching service that you can use to store static and dynamic web content that uses TCP.For more information about content caching, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.htmlWhat Is Amazon CloudFront?https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html /a

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure the application to use an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Latency-based routing policies improve network performance only when resources exist in multiple Regions. The company currently hosts the application in only eu-central-1. With a latency-based routing policy, all North American traffic would continue to go to eu-central-1. Performance would not improve.For more information about DNS routing policies, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.htmlLatency-Based Routing.

question_content: An application team has started using Amazon EMR to run batch jobs, using datasets located in Amazon S3. During the initial testing of the workload, a solutions architect notices that the account is starting to accrue NAT gateway data processing costs.How can the team optimize the cost of the workload?

answer_choices.choice_content: Detach the NAT gateway from the subnet where the Amazon EMR clusters are running.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. If the clusters run in a private subnet without a NAT gateway or an alternative method to reach the S3 bucket, the workload will not be able to reach the objects in Amazon S3 and will fail.For more information about how to access S3 buckets, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-bucket-intro.htmlAccessing a bucket.

answer_choices.choice_content: Replace the NAT gateway with a customer gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A customer gateway is a physical or software appliance that you own or manage in your on-premises network (on your side of an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection). A customer gateway is not related to communication between a VPC and an AWS service such as Amazon S3.For more information about customer gateways, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/your-cgw.htmlYour customer gateway device.

answer_choices.choice_content: Replace the NAT gateway with an S3 VPC endpoint.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. An S3 VPC endpoint is a gateway endpoint that does not incur a charge for traffic to Amazon S3.For more information about gateway VPC endpoints, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpce-gateway.html#gateway-endpoint-pricingPricing for gateway endpoints.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a network ACL on the subnets where the Amazon EMR clusters are running to open access to Amazon S3.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution is not applicable because by default, a network ACL does not block outbound traffic. A network ACL will not help with the NAT gateway costs.For more information about network ACLs, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.htmlNetwork ACLs.

question_content: A company stops a cluster of Amazon EC2 instances over a weekend. The costs decrease, but they do not drop to zero.Which resources could still be generating costs? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: Elastic IP addresses
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. To ensure efficient use of Elastic IP addresses, AWS imposes a small hourly charge if an Elastic IP address is not associated with a running instance, or if an Elastic IP address is associated with a stopped instance or an unattached network interface. For this reason, if an EC2 instance is in a stopped state but still has an associated Elastic IP address, the EC2 instance still will incur charges.For more information about Elastic IP addresses, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/elastic-ip-addresses-eip.htmlElastic IP addresses.

answer_choices.choice_content: Data transfer out
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS imposes charges for each EC2 instance's data in and data out at corresponding data transfer rates. Additionally, data transfers between AWS services in different AWS Regions incur charges at standard inter-Region data transfer rates. However, stopped EC2 instances cannot accept or send network traffic. Therefore, stopped EC2 instances cannot generate data transfer out. This option could not be the cause of the charges.For more information about the EC2 instance lifecycle, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.htmlInstance lifecycle. For more information about EC2 pricing, see https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/Amazon EC2 pricing.

answer_choices.choice_content: Regional data transfers
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS imposes charges for each EC2 instance's data in and data out at corresponding data transfer rates. Additionally, data transfers between AWS services in different AWS Regions incur charges at standard inter-Region data transfer rates. However, stopped EC2 instances cannot accept or send network traffic. Therefore, stopped EC2 instances cannot generate data transfer out. This option could not be the cause of the charges.For more information about the EC2 instance lifecycle, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.htmlInstance lifecycle. For more information about EC2 pricing, see https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/Amazon EC2 pricing.

answer_choices.choice_content: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. EBS volumes can be provisioned, managed, and billed separately from EC2 instances. If you stop or terminate an EC2 instance, any EBS volumes that are in use can be retained as persistent storage beyond the lifecycle of the EC2 instance.Amazon EBS incurs costs for the amount of storage that is provisioned to your account (measured in gigabyte-months). EC2 instances accrue charges only while they are running, but EBS volumes that are provisioned in the account to instances continue to accrue charges even when the volumes are not in use.For more information about EBS pricing, see https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/Amazon EBS pricing.

answer_choices.choice_content: AWS Auto Scaling
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. There is no additional charge for AWS Auto Scaling. You pay only for the AWS resources that you need to run your applications, as well as Amazon CloudWatch monitoring fees. Therefore, you will not incur charges for AWS Auto Scaling, but you might incur charges for other resources that are used in the AWS Auto Scaling process.For more information about AWS Auto Scaling pricing, see https://aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/pricing/AWS Auto Scaling Pricing.
